correctness.rationale: The normalized Hardy reproducing kernel gives z=(1-t)/(1-a t e^{iψ}); m>=2 makes phase ψ cover the circle for any λ phase. The inverse u=(1-z)/z=s(1-ae^{iψ}) sweeps exactly the closed sector Re u≥sqrt(1-a²)|u| for 0<a<1 via the positive quadratic root. Möbius inversion gives intersection of the two closed disks centered at 1/2±i√(1-a²)/(2a), radius 1/(2a), omitting origin. The origin is an extreme point so the punctured lens stays convex. Chord area and arc length give the stated A, P, H. For a=0 the range is (0,1]; for a=1 the open diameter disk plus {1}, because u in right half-plane except origin. Independent chord quadrature at a=.1,.5,.9 reproduces exact areas and finite phase samples lie in both disks. Finite samples are corroboration, not complete image equality.
